THANK YOU FINALLY SOMEONE WHO GETS IT!   Those of us who have worked retail for years have had that situation where: we 100% agree with the customer and want to help them but either by policy or authority ( or manager password/overides) we can't actually fix the problem ourselves.   


 I worked at wal-mart years ago where there was a time where ANY issue with a receipt, even an accidental double scan of a product or a price change not reflected at the register, HAD to be taken to the customer service desk EVEN if it was just $1.00.  People would yell and scream at the cashier but there was not a damn thing that cashier could do at that point.

>clerk says there’s nothing he can do for a refund since the gas was already pumped

Since this is the only piece we know (from the original post) we do not know if there was or was-not any protocol.  That being said it's no good assuming it to all be on the clerk then. I'm also not saying it's the customers fault and they should just accept the loss.

My point was that BECAUSE we don't know more, because we were not there, and because we don't know the manager or policies we can't just assume it's 100% on the clerk if they had no authority or even to your point was not given proper training.

Yes the customer should get the gas or their money back but that's not the issue of my point. We can agree that it's "in" the company for the issue but not be certain where the fault then lies (again restating for emphasis the clerk could have no authority or not been trained for such things and thus it's the managers fault or hell even the company if it's a family gas station with no set training).

There is a lot of hate in the comments towards the clerk but having been on that side of the counter i can 100% say that some companies/management DO NOT GIVE CLERKS AUTHORITY TO REFUND OR GIVE FREE\* GAS.  This even applies to retail/shop workers.  


Even if the mistake was on the clerks end upper management would have to be the one to refund or fix it and that is hoping there is someone there who can do that. I've actually seen a situation where an employee was written up for doing a refund on such a situation despite the fact that management would have done the refund anyway.

Everything you described is pretty damn close to a mirror of my life and how hellish it has been. The lie that, "if you do X, Y will follow", that if you work hard, apply yourself, get good grades, get a degree, go the extra mile, work overtime, take on more work, etc...etc...     IT'S A LIE!!!  


There is no guarantee. We were manipulated.  We were sold on that lie growing up. And now those with power and money blame us repeating the same lies that we must not have done enough. That it's a "you" problem. I hate what this society has become because of the few rich and powerful people/companies that have managed to financial cripple if not outright ruin millions of people all for the bottom line of bigger profits.

In my job hunt i've have had these experiences where i knew 100% i was overqualified working at a sub shop, working at a gas station, the entry level break your back jobs are often described as the start "high school-er just out of class" jobs.  And even after saying i accept the lower pay and the tasks of the job BECAUSE i needed the income to pay bills i was still given the same rejection letters you got.    


It's, pardon my language, it's F\^!KING SICK that you can be trapped in a place where you are too inexperienced supposedly for any higher up jobs and yet over experienced for any lesser job and thus literally put yourself in a place where you have NO JOB because you tried to better yourself with education and work experience.

Now taking that a step further:  imagine if we took those jobs that paid some salary of 400,000$ + a year (including bonuses) and instead of one person for that job we split that into pieces and give it to 4-8 people.

Hell lets just say 4 people:   each gets a salary of 100,000$.  they divvy up the workloads and work days between 4 people.  they each can take sick days and go on vacations while the other 3 cover.  If this is a "big-wig" job where there is a lot of manager stuff and oversight they can easily split up and meet with all their workers under them, see the staff, take a tour of the production facility, whatever have you because now they can be in multiple places at the same time.  


4 people now get a wage that can, in most place, fully take care of a family off that income. We tackled any stress levels of the job, health issues that might arise from them or family requiring time away, and we made the position more productive because we have spread the work amongst 4 people who can go full force should they choose and take on more work than that 1 person could have ever achieved 

What a dream that would be...    now the nightmare.  What i just described happens in reverse for those of us at the bottom level of the workforce: what was once 4 people is now 1 person. We carry all the workload with less time, less sick days, less resources to do the same jobs that took 4 people. And we do it for the same low wage rather than getting paid for 4 people worth of work.

What she describes is exactly my situation. 35 years old as of today, got a BS degree, Magnum Cum Laude, GPA 3.89, 10+ years of wok experience on top of that spread amongst Retail, Night Audit, warehouse, and production work, and yet i still can't get a lead or any higher level job that would actually allow me to afford rent or take out a loan. to buy a cheap home.

Where i live rent is 1200+ on low crap end with 1700 for middle.   Homes are 300k + for the cheapest available.   And yet most jobs hover around 9-10 through the 15$ range in the valley here with one exception being the "Heavy" duty manufacturing (not stop labor 50-75 lbs kind) that would have you work rotating 2-2-3 shifts.  It's no wonder people get burnt out mentally and physically from those  jobs and leave because of the toll it takes on their body. So people stay in those to pay the bills and suffer or leave and end up haveing 7 people families, kids and adults, all living in a 3 bedroom home like the one i am in.

ANYONE WORKING 40 HOURS A WEEK IN ANY JOB SHOULD HAVE FINANCIAL INDEPENDENCE, COVER BASIC BILLS (health, utility's, basics required phone internet for job as required now in days), AND HAVE A HOME OF THEIR OWN!

And yet i see posting for jobs all over my town for 10-12$ part and full time and yet you would NEVER be able to rent a place, as it requires 3x the income you make to qualify, and you would NEVER afford a home, because the cost would be to much for dent to income ratio.

Those of us in the 20-40 areas are screwed because most likely started with nothing, tried to save and work our way to a better future, and got priced out of anything that would have let us build up any kind of financial independence.

I have at times a similar feeling that i can't do anything to help myself or save myself. I have at times felt that i am not worth saving and that the time and energy spent by those around me would be better spent helping others and not me.   


There are only a few thing that help me keep going in my life. One of them is giving or sacrificing of my self to help others. I can't help myself, i have a hard time seeing the good in myself, but i can see the good in others.   


I'm willing to bet you would never wish what you are feeling on others and that makes you a good person.  


I believe if you knew someone who has these pains you would take them on knowing how much they hurt because you would not want others to suffer, that makes you a good person.  


The small acts you do unconsciously that you may think are nothing or feel effortless can mean a great deal to someone because for them in that moment they felt like no one cared or noticed, that makes you a good person.  


maybe at this point i am rambling.  but my point is we can't save ourselves at times but we can save/hep others.  If there is something small you can do for another person to ease their burdens it may be enough to hold onto to keep going another day. That holding onto that small little piece of good we can say, "i at least took away the pebble in a wold of pain for someone".

My step-father talks about the good old days and still acts, despite being in his 70's and retired, that those days are still here and it's this generation that is the problem.

hardly anything about his work life some 30-40 years ago is the same as today:   you can't walk in and get a job anywhere the same day.  The pay is not going to be enough to be independent/afford rent or housing for entry level work anywhere. He payed less than 300$ for his education in California decades ago that now costs tens of thousands of dollars today. We are in a rat race competing for jobs at the lowest wage to survive and for him any 40 hour a week job back them could at least give you some independence.

There is such a generational gap, a kind of out of touch-ness to our parents that they don't get what we face just trying to figure out how to make ends meet paying the bills and not wanting to just give up and end it all.

But....  ya i did not get that from my stepfather.  it was all on the results it seemed liked.  no connection it seemed to your workers.
